newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - European bonds rally, glow comes off shares.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - European bonds rally, glow comes off shares.

text.p: European bond markets rallied strongly on Thursday but the glow came off shares ahead of potentially-troubling U.S. payrolls figures due on Friday.
With German markets closed for the country's reunification holiday, foreign exchange markets were relatively quiet and bonds stole the limelight.

Italian bonds soared to new peaks, made more attractive by the Bank of Spain shaving half a percentage point off its main money market rate. Portugal later cut its money market rate by 0.15 percentage points.
French and British government bonds also rallied strongly, with some analysts saying European debt markets could weather poor U.S. jobs figures.
"There is reason to believe that a decoupling (of U.S. and European bonds) is under way at the moment," said Ken Wattret, economist at Paribas Capital Markets.

Analysts said the September non-farm payrolls number due on Friday would attract the usual close attention but its transatlantic impact should be less than in the past, when a strong figure has prompted turmoil in the markets.
Although expectations of low U.S. jobs growth has been building up, bond market analysts said there was still scope for disappointment if the outcome exceeded the consensus forecast.
London share traders said the U.S. data was a major reason why investors took a back seat despite the blue chip FTSE index briefly pushing to a new high in early trade

"There's always nervousness before those figures but as long as the bond markets continue to hold up well, there's no reason for the FTSE to slip further...although the potential above 4,000 looks a bit limited," one trader said.
The index popped up to a trading record of 4,024.3 in early business before sliding below the 4,000 watershed it crossed for the first time on Wednesday. French stocks also fell.

London went back through 4,000 as Wall Street opened in positive ground amid further signs of slowing U.S. industrial activity. Commerce Department figures showed factory orders dropped at the sharpest rate in 3-1/2 years during August.
French stocks also picked themselves off their lows after Wall Street opened after consolidating Wednesday's 0.88 percent gain.
"We seem to have run out of steam around the 2,150 ceiling. Volume is very disappointing with Germany closed today," one broker said.
The dollar steadied above opening levels in the European afternoon, with dealers seeing the dollar well bid on any dips in its value.
Activity was muted, partly due to the German holiday, but more from a general reluctance to continue the dollar's recent rise ahead of the jobs report.
"People are wary about taking the dollar higher ahead of tomorrow, especially when you consider the extreme reaction the payrolls numbers can generate," said a Swiss bank dealer.
"There is still a big question mark over which way the dollar will travel if the figures are outside expectations."
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 111.58 yen and 1.5327 marks versus Wednesday's late European levels of 111.75 and 1.5277.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1400 GMT
London - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading shares was down 15.1 points at 4,000.00.
Paris - The CAC-40 share index was down 4.50 points at 2,137.34.
Frankfurt - The market was closed for a holiday. The 30-share DAX index closed on Wednesday at 2,676.5.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed slightly easier at $378.85 against $379.50 in the morning. Silver was off four cents at $4.89.
